adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — [P2, confidence 100, Blocking] "new Thread(() -> {" Starting the reader without a readiness barrier leaves deletion unordered against the first read, so the test accepts an execution in which all deletions finish before the worker begins and never exercises concurrent access.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test design issue in the new test code. The test starts a reader thread with `new Thread(() -> {...}).start()` and immediately proceeds to delete groups without any synchronization to ensure the reader thread has started and performed at least one read. This means there's a race condition where all deletions could complete before the reader thread even begins executing, which would mean the test never actually exercises concurrent read/delete access as intended. This is a valid concern about test effectiveness, not a bug in production code, but it's a specific, actionable issue with the new test code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:157 — [P2, confidence 100, Blocking] "assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());" Because no thread handle is retained or joined, this assertion has no happens-before relation with worker termination and therefore excludes any in-flight-request exception appended after it, producing a false pass for that execution.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in the test. The test starts a thread that reads groups while the main thread deletes them. After deletion completes, `deletedAll.set(true)` is called and then immediately `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` is executed. However, there's no `Thread.join()` or other synchronization to ensure the worker thread has actually terminated before the assertion runs. The worker thread could still be in the middle of a `groups()` call when the assertion executes, and any exception thrown after the assertion would not be caught. This is a real concurrency bug in the test code that could cause false passes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:157 — [P1, confidence 100, Blocking] "assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());" This assertion runs without a reader-start barrier or a join, so it passes when the reader has not executed or has not yet recorded a failing concurrent request and gives false confidence in the NPE fix.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in the test. Looking at the diff, the test starts a reader thread that loops while `!deletedAll.get()`, then the main thread deletes groups and sets `deletedAll.set(true)`. The assertion `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs immediately after setting the flag, but there's no `Thread.join()` or synchronization barrier to ensure the reader thread has actually executed any iterations or completed. The reader thread could: (1) not have started yet, (2) be in the middle of a request when deletedAll becomes true and exit before recording an exception, or (3) have recorded exceptions that aren't visible due to memory visibility issues. This is a real test defect that could cause false positives.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — [P2, confidence 100, Advisory] "new Thread(() -> {" This non-daemon reader thread is never joined or otherwise managed, so an in-flight read that completes after the method returns continues against fixtures during teardown or a later test and makes suite behavior order-dependent.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test creates a new Thread at line 139 that is never joined. The thread runs a while loop checking `deletedAll.get()`, and while `deletedAll.set(true)` is called after deleting groups, there's no `thread.join()` to wait for the thread to complete. This means the thread could still be executing (making API calls to `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups()`) after the test method returns, potentially interfering with test teardown or subsequent tests. This is a real concurrency bug in the test code.
